newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian annual inflation slows to record low.
newsitem.headline: Russian annual inflation slows to record low.

text.p: Russia's annual inflation rate slowed to a record low in December, official figures released Monday showed, and financial analysts said the government's 1997 inflation target of 1 percent a month looked realistic.

The State Statistics Committee said the rise in consumer prices had slowed to 1.4 percent in December from 1.9 percent in November, bringing the year-on-year rate for the month -- and the headline rate for the year -- down to a post-reform low of 21.8 percent.
The year-on-year rate was 24.0 percent in November and 131 percent in December 1995.
In the 1997 budget, which is still awaiting final approval by deputies, the government is counting on a further halving in the annual inflation rate to 11.8 percent.
"The government is planning low inflation of about 1 percent a month through 1997. I think that's a realistic target," said Robert Devane, head of fixed-income sales and trading at Troika Dialogue.
The slowdown in inflation is one of the brightest spots on the government's economic record for 1996, when the economy fell another 5-6 percent.
Many companies were unable or unwilling to pay their bills last year, and the resulting tax shortfall caused the International Monetary Fund to suspend payments of its $10 billion loan to Russia.
Tax revenues have now picked up again and the IMF has resumed lending, but the government was only able to prevent an inflationary ballooning in the budget deficit by slashing spending.
As a result, many salaries and pensions have gone unpaid, creating a political problem for President Boris Yeltsin on his return to the Kremlin last month from heart surgery.
The inflation figures, which were in line with expectations, had little impact on financial markets.
